phguide.title: Test your soil pH
phguide.zigzag: Walk across the field in a zigzag. Take soil from at least 15 spots.
phguide.skip: Skip odd spots: near trees, on paths, or where fertiliser or lime spilled.
phguide.dig: Scrape off plant waste. Dig to 6 inches (15 cm), the same depth each time.
phguide.mix: Put all the soil in a clean bucket. Let it dry, then mix it well.
phguide.water: Put the mixed soil and water in the kit's tube, as much as the kit says.
phguide.shake: Shake it, then wait as long as the kit says.
phguide.colour: Match the colour to the kit's chart. Read the number next to it.
phguide.type: Type that number into Soil test pH.
phguide.again: Test each field every 3 years, or once per crop rotation. Not sure? Ask your township extension officer.
phguide.source: Sampling steps: Mississippi State University Extension, Soil Testing for the Farmer.

fp.hintSteps: 6 short steps, one question at a time
fp.q1sub: Pick one. This decides what is best for you. You can change it later.
fp.p.money.t: Get a good price at the market
fp.p.money.d: More cash in hand after the harvest
fp.p.soil.t: Farm this land for many years
fp.p.soil.d: Not just this year: keep the soil good so it feeds the family year after year
fp.p.water.d: Ponds and wells run low in the dry season; grow with very little water
fp.p.safe.t: Don't lose if the weather turns
fp.p.safe.d: Even if rain fails or a flood comes, get your costs back
fp.trade.money: The best-paying crop may need a lot of fertiliser. Still put the price first?
fp.trade.soil: The crop that keeps the soil good may pay a bit less this season. Still put the land first?
fp.trade.water: Black gram pays a bit less but needs little water and keeps the soil good. Still put water first?
fp.trade.safe: Playing safe may mean not the highest price. Still put not losing first?
fp.tradeSub: A choice only counts if it still stands when it costs something.
fp.q2: What did the weather do to your field?
fp.q2sub: Last season, or what you fear this year. Tap all that happened.
fp.d.flood.d: Water came into the field and stayed
fp.d.drought.d: Rain came late, or stopped early
fp.d.pest.d: Pests or disease hit everything at once
fp.stays.q: Does water stay long in your field?
fp.stays.d: If it does, pulses are sown later, after the water goes down.
fp.q2hint: The satellite checks some of these. If it disagrees with you, step 5 shows it.
fp.q3: Prices keep rising. What hits you?
fp.q3sub: No price numbers to type. “Not sure” never blocks you.
fp.pr.fert.d: A bag of urea costs more than last year
fp.pr.seed.q: Is seed expensive, or hard to find?
fp.pr.seed.d: Good seed is not in the shop, or costs too much
fp.pr.fuel.q: Are diesel and day wages up?
fp.pr.fuel.d: Diesel, tractor hire and day wages cost more
fp.pr.sell.d: Buyers push the price down at harvest
fp.q4: What do you have, and what is short?
fp.q4sub: These decide what is possible. A plan that needs what you don't have is not a plan.
fp.w.q: In the dry season, will your pond, well or canal water this field?
fp.w.d: Rice in the dry season needs water all the way through
fp.l.labour.d: No day labour, family hands only
fp.l.machine.q: Is it hard to hire a tractor?
fp.l.machine.d: Hire is expensive, or it is never your turn
fp.l.pesticide.d: The shop has none, or it costs too much
fp.l.cash.q: Is money tight, or a loan due?
fp.l.cash.d: If so, low-cost crops come first
fp.q4hint: Only you know these. No satellite can see them.
fp.q5: We have already looked at your field
fp.q5sub: Nothing to fill in. This comes from the map and NASA satellites.
fp.f.moist: Soil wetness in the root zone
fp.f.near: Grid-cell values near {town}, not a measurement in your field.
fp.chk.money_no_prices: You put the price first, but no selling prices are known, so income is left out of the score. We say it, not hide it. Add your prices under Details to include it.
fp.chk.water_but_wet: You want to save water, and the field is wet now (wetness {g}). Water still runs short later in the dry season, so your choice can stand. You decide.
fp.chk.flood_agrees: You reported a flood, and the satellite agrees: wetness {g}, {rain} mm of rain in 30 days ({above} mm above normal). Sowing waits for the water to go down.
fp.chk.drought_but_wet: You reported drought or late rain, but this field is wet now ({g}) after {rain} mm of rain this month. The drought may be last season's. This dry season is only treated as short of water if you said your water is little or none.
fp.chk.none_but_wet_month: You said nothing happened, but the satellite shows a very wet month: {rain} mm, {above} mm above normal. Check for standing water before sowing.
fp.chk.water_vs_record: The field record says dry-season water is “{record}”. You said “{said}”. Your answer is used.
fp.chk.no_moisture: No soil wetness reading for this field, so moisture is not scored. It is listed as missing.
fp.q6sub: Fix anything that is wrong. No answer is shown until you confirm.

fp.l.localLead: You told us these. The score does not use them yet, so check them before you decide:
fp.ns.d_storm: Storms are not in the score. Ask about short, sturdy varieties.
fp.ns.d_heat: The score checks 30 years of average heat, not single heat waves.
fp.ns.d_erosion: Check the bank and the topsoil before sowing.
fp.ns.p_seed: Make sure seed is in your township shop before you decide.
fp.ns.p_fuel: Machine passes and hired hands are not in the score.
fp.ns.p_sell: Ask buyers about the price before you sow. Storage is not in the score.
fp.ns.l_labour: How many hands each crop needs is not in the score.
fp.ns.l_machine: Land preparation is not in the score.

fp.rule.water_low: It needs little water in the dry season.
fp.rule.water_very_high: It needs a lot of water when water is scarce.
fp.rule.irrigated_crop_unavailable: It needs water all season, and you have little or none.
fp.rule.irrigated_crop_sometimes: It needs water all season, and you only have some.
fp.rule.irrigated_crop_available: It needs water all season, and you have enough.
fp.rule.rainfed_crop_irrigation_availabl: Your water is a backup if a dry spell comes.
fp.rule.moisture_normal: It can start on the moisture left after rice.
fp.rule.moisture_low_irrigation_unavaila: The soil is dry and there is no water: it may not start.
fp.rule.moisture_low_irrigation_sometime: The soil is dry and water is uncertain: it may start poorly.

fp.rule.moisture_low_irrigated_crop: The soil is dry, so it needs more water from the start.
fp.rule.harvest_clear: It is harvested well before the pre-monsoon rain.
fp.rule.harvest_near_onset: It is harvested close to the pre-monsoon rain.
fp.rule.harvest_after_onset: It is harvested after the rain starts: risk of a wet harvest.

fp.rule.drainage_good: Your field drains well, which it needs.
fp.rule.drainage_poor: Water stays in your field, and it hates wet feet.
